### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

### Describe the bug

After #27928, installing an **unsigned** (`SECURE_UPGRADE_MODE=no_sign`) SONiC image in **UEFI** mode **from ONIE** no longer creates an EFI NVRAM boot entry for SONiC. The firmware then falls back to booting ONIE, so the machine never boots the freshly installed SONiC.

For the UEFI VS image added in #27080, this makes the build's UEFI boot verification (`check_install.py`) time out — i.e. a **blocking build failure** on the default (unsigned)VS UEFI build.

### Root cause

In `installer/default_platform.conf`, `demo_install_uefi_grub()` does:

```sh
grub-install --no-nvram ...          # deliberately no NVRAM entry, and no --removable fallback
if [ "$install_env" = "sonic" ]; then
    efibootmgr --quiet --create ...  # the ONLY code that registers the SONiC UEFI boot entry
fi
```

#27928 (commit `e57ada5e3`) wrapped the previously **unconditional** `efibootmgr --create` in `if [ "$install_env" = "sonic" ]`. When installing from ONIE (`install_env=onie`):

- `grub-install --no-nvram` writes no NVRAM entry, and without `--removable` there is no `\EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI` fallback either;
- the `efibootmgr --create` block is skipped;
- nothing else creates an entry (ONIE does not create a boot entry for the NOS — that is the NOS installer's job).

Result: no SONiC `BootXXXX` entry exists, so the firmware boots the only remaining entry — ONIE's `\EFI\onie\shimx64.efi` — landing in ONIE.

**Signed** images are unaffected: they take `demo_install_uefi_shim()`, which still creates the entry unconditionally.
grub-install --no-nvram ...          # deliberately no NVRAM entry, and no --removable fallback
if [ "$install_env" = "sonic" ]; then
    efibootmgr --quiet --create ...  # the ONLY code that registers the SONiC UEFI boot entry
fi
```

### Steps to Reproduce

### Steps to reproduce

Build the default (unsigned) UEFI VS image on current master:

```
make configure PLATFORM=vs
make target/sonic-vs.img.gz     # runs `generate_kvm_image 1 UEFI`
```

The UEFI verify boot lands in ONIE and `check_install.py` times out.

So the UEFI-from-ONIE verify was last exercised before the gate existed; the two changes were never run together in CI.

### Additional evidence (reproduced locally)

Building the UEFI KVM image with the gate present, the verify boot loads `Boot0004 "ONIE" … \EFI\onie\shimx64.efi` and times out. With `efibootmgr --create` also allowed for `install_env=onie`, the install creates `Boot0005 "SONiC-OS" … \EFI\SONiC-OS\grubx64.efi`, and the verify boot reaches `sonic login:` and the build succeeds. Same tree, same OVMF firmware — the only difference is the `install_env` gate.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

### Expected behavior

An unsigned UEFI image installed from ONIE should register an EFI boot entry and boot SONiC, as it did before #27928.

### Why CI did not catch it

- #27928 (the gate) merged 2026-07-09.
- #27080 (which added `generate_kvm_image 1 UEFI` + the OVMF verify for the unsigned VS image) last ran Azure CI on 2026-07-06 and merged 2026-07-11 on approval, with no CI re-run after 2026-07-09.

resolution.title: Fix UEFI boot entry not created for images installed from ONIE (regression from #27928)
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it

Fixes #28382.

After #27928, installing an **unsigned** (`SECURE_UPGRADE_MODE=no_sign`) SONiC image in **UEFI** mode **from ONIE** no longer creates an EFI NVRAM boot entry for SONiC, so the firmware falls back to booting ONIE and never boots the freshly installed SONiC. For the UEFI VS image added in #27080 this makes the build's UEFI boot verification (`check_install.py`) time out.

Root cause: in `installer/default_platform.conf`, `demo_install_uefi_grub()` runs `grub-install --no-nvram` (no NVRAM entry, and no `--removable` fallback), and #27928 (commit `e57ada5e3`) wrapped the previously **unconditional** `efibootmgr --create` — the only code that registers the SONiC UEFI boot entry — in `if [ "$install_env" = "sonic" ]`. When installing from ONIE (`install_env=onie`) that block is skipped and nothing else creates an entry, so the only remaining entry (ONIE's `\EFI\onie\shimx64.efi`) is booted. Signed images are unaffected because they use `demo_install_uefi_shim()`, which still creates the entry unconditionally.

#### How I did it

Allow the `efibootmgr --create` boot entry to be created for the `onie` install environment as well. Only `build` (a chroot with no EFI NVRAM) must be excluded, so the guard becomes `if [ "$install_env" = "sonic" ] || [ "$install_env" = "onie" ]`.

#### How to verify it

Build the default (unsigned) UEFI VS image, which runs `generate_kvm_image 1 UEFI`:

```
make configure PLATFORM=vs
make target/sonic-vs.img.gz
```

- **Before:** the UEFI verify boot loads `Boot0004 "ONIE" … \EFI\onie\shimx64.efi` and `check_install.py` times out.
- **After:** the install creates `Boot0005 "SONiC-OS" … \EFI\SONiC-OS\grubx64.efi`, the verify boot reaches `sonic login:`, and the build succeeds.
